text:
Alex: quick design review — attaching screenshots in Figma but TL;DR: the pool chooser + min/max + burst explainer feels visually noisy when the SLO slider is set low. can we try an inline explainer that collapses?
Maria: +1. current tooltip for burst is like a paragraph. people skip it. can we do a 1-line affordance with a 'learn more' link? :thinking_face:
Ken: agree. my main worry is discoverability for non-technical PMs. they need to know burst is temporary capacity that can exceed max. suggestion: label badge 'Burst (temporary)' and on hover show: "Burst runs when requests > capacity for up to X mins".
Jamie: small a11y note — hover-only affordances are bad for keyboard/screen reader users. make sure there's a visible hint and an inline help icon with aria-label.
Alex: good call. prototype idea: show condensed line under pool name: "Min 2 • Max 8 • Burst +4". clicking the "Burst" token expands a small panel with details and an inline example of cost impact.
Maria: Love condensed line. for the SLO slider, the visual weight is too strong — it pulls attention away from the pool selector. can we reduce contrast and add a microcopy line: "SLO = target latency percentile"? it's confusing what the knob maps to.
Ken: wording suggestion for microcopy: "SLO: tail latency target (ms) — higher = stricter". maybe add an info icon that toggles an example traffic curve.
UXBot: accessibility check: ensure slider has aria-valuetext="SLO target: {value} milliseconds" and keyboard step increments of 5ms.
Jamie: re: keyboard, also ensure pool chips are tabbable and have clear focus ring. current Figma shows faint outline. bump to 3px and use color token --focus-strong.
Maria: copy tweak — users confuse 'max' with 'burst cap'. maybe rename 'Max' to 'Reserved Max' or 'Guaranteed max' and keep 'Burst' separate. Thoughts?
Ken: I'd avoid 'Guaranteed' — that implies contract. 'Reserved max' is ok but long. How about 'Capacity cap' vs 'Burst buffer'?
Alex: we need short labels. proposals: 'Min', 'Target', 'Max', 'Burst'. but add a tooltip for 'Max: sustained capacity'. keep 'Burst' definition visible in expanded panel.
Jamie: on the expanded panel, show a tiny timeline example: 0–2m normal -> spike -> burst uses +4 for up to 5m -> rollback. even an inline ascii graph helps.
Maria: also, can we show estimated cost delta next to burst in the panel? e.g., "Estimated +18% cost at peak" so teams see tradeoffs.
Ken: technical question for eng — how precise can we make that estimate? if it's a wide range we should say "estimate" and link to docs.
Alex: engineering can compute rolling-window extra GPU time. we'll show a ballpark and link to cost calc. UI copy: "Estimated cost: ~+15–25% during spike. See details."
UXBot: accessibility quick: color contrast for red warning badges fails at small sizes. use token --warning-strong and ensure AA contrast.
Jamie: final nit — when SLO slider is at extreme (very strict) we should auto-suggest increasing min or reducing burst. maybe a subtle inline suggestion pill: "Suggested: raise Min to 4" with accept button. this reduces surprise.
Maria: love that. can it be non-modal and reversible? just a one-click apply and small toast.
Ken: agreed. and we need guardrail copy: if user applies auto-suggest, show what will change and a way to preview cost delta before commit.
Alex: ok action items: 1) design: condensed pool line + tappable Burst token + expanded panel mock w/ ascii timeline + cost estimate (Maria/Jamie) 2) copy: microcopy variants for 'Max' and 'Burst' (Maria/Ken) 3) dev: aria-labels for slider and chips, keyboard flow, and cost calc hook (Ken/Eng) 4) prototype: one-click suggestion pill with preview toast (Alex/Jamie).
Maria: timeline? can we get mocks by EOD tomorrow?
Jamie: I'll do an initial pass in the morning, pinging @Alex for review.
Ken: I'll scope aria changes and a rough cost endpoint we can hit in staging.
Alex: thanks all — leaving comments in Figma and will follow up in product sync. :thumbsup:
